The new Mercedes-Benz EQS 450+ covered 539 miles without stopping to charge, making range anxiety look like a thing of the past.
Mercedes EQS beats EPA range in real-world test
Mercedes-Benz overhauled the EQS electric sedan , including a bigger battery and an 800V electrical architecture.
The 2027 Mercedes-Benz EQS 450+ uses a 122 kWh battery that provides an EPA-estimated range of up to 467 miles.
While that’s already impressive, the electric sedan will likely go even farther in everyday driving conditions. During Edmunds recent EV Range Test , the 2027 Mercedes EQS 450+ drove a whopping 539 miles without stopping to charge.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
The EQS beat its own EPA estimate by 72 miles and is now the longest-range electric sedan Edmunds has ever tested, beating the Lucid Air, the first EV to break the 500-mile mark. The only EV that has it beat is the Cadillac Escalade IQ, which managed 558 miles from its massive 205 kWh battery.
Mercedes-Benz EQS 580 4MATIC (Source: Mercedes-Benz)
During the test, the 2027 Mercedes EQS 450+ was also more efficient than its official numbers suggest.
The new EQS used 29.6 kWh per 100 miles, beating its EPA estimate of 28 kWh per 100 miles. In comparison, the 2025 Mercedes EQS 450+ covered 464 miles and used 34 kWh per 100 miles during the same test, so the improvements are considerable.
Edmunds observed a peak charging rate of 350 kW, in line with Mercedes’ estimates, while it sustained an average of 222 kW throughout the session.
Mercedes-Benz EQS 580 4MATIC (Source: Mercedes-Benz)
Both beat the older EQS, which reached a peak charge rate of 208 kW and sustained an average of 175 kW.
The new Mercedes EQS 450+ added 825 miles of range in an hour, and 100 miles in just over 7 minutes, nearly twice the speed of the 2025MY.
The Edmunds EV Range Test is designed to provide a more accurate estimate of an EV’s range in everyday driving conditions. It includes 60% city and 40% highway driving with an average speed of 40 mph. The vehicle stays within 5 mph of the posted speed limit, and the climate control is set to auto at 72 degrees.
Electrek’s Take
How much is too much? 539 miles on a single charge is impressive, but do you need it? In a recent “nationally representative” survey , BMW found that Americans want more EV range than they actually need.
The study showed that 73% consider 25, 50, or 75 miles enough to cover their daily driving. However, 42% said they would require at least 300 miles of range before they would consider an EV.
If you have access to a home charger, nothing beats waking up with a full charge every day. Meanwhile, public charging continues to improve, giving EV drivers more reliable options on longer trips.
Faster charging also helps. Another 53% said they would be more likely to consider an EV if it could add about 150 miles of range in around 10 minutes.
In the same Edmunds EV Range Test last week, the new 2027 BMW iX3 50 xDrive drove 436 miles on a single charge, exceeding its EPA estimate of 392 miles by 44 miles. It also used 28.3 kWh per 100 miles during the test, beating its official EPA estimate of 32 kWh per 100 miles.
Top comment by Dan B
Liked by 3 people
I'm really glad to see more articles like this and people talking more about efficiency. It's not just about bigger batteries and range. It needs to be about smaller batteries plus great efficiency giving that same range. We need to do this with more efficient designs, more sedans and lighter vehicles.
But good job MB.
View all comments
The new 2027 Volvo EX60 drove 352 miles while the 2027 Mercedes-Benz GLC Electric covered 392 miles during the same test.
One thing is certain: electric vehicles are becoming more efficient, enabling longer driving ranges and faster charging times. As battery tech advances, EVs will drive farther and charge faster, while safety and performance will continue to improve.

Agnico Eagle Mines CEO Amar Al-Joundi speaks at the Capital Projects Symposium in Toronto. Credit: Blair McBride
Posted By: Blair McBride November 9, 2026
Agnico Eagle Mines (TSX, NYSE: AEM), Canada’s top gold producer is willing to spend more and wait longer before committing to new mines to avoid costly surprises during construction, CEO Ammar Al-Joundi says.
Agnico’s history offers a guide to what can go wrong. Higher-than-expected operating costs and lower ore grades at its Meadowbank mine in Nunavut prompted a $645-million (C$910-million) after-tax writedown in 2011. That same year, Agnico recorded a $161-million writedown at Goldex in Quebec after rock stability concerns forced a suspension of production. Al-Joundi didn’t explicitly link today’s approach to those setbacks.
“Most of our peers will do 30 or 40% detailed engineering before they announce a project,” Al-Joundi said Monday at the Canadian Institute of Mining, Metallurgy and Petroleum’s (CIM) Capital Projects Symposium in Toronto.
“The disadvantage of getting to the higher engineering is it costs you more and it delays the announcement. The big advantage is it materially reduces your risk. It doesn’t eliminate it, but it reduces a lot of risk.”
Agnico aims to complete 60% to 70% of detailed engineering before approving construction, compared with the 30% to 40% most peers complete before announcing projects, the CEO said. In an industry dogged by budget overruns and delays, that extra preparation is intended to make cost estimates more reliable and build investors’ confidence that the company can deliver.
Trust over risk
Agnico’s approach addresses one of the mining industry’s most persistent problems: projects that run over budget or fall behind schedule as unforeseen engineering, construction and logistical challenges emerge.
By completing more engineering and securing key permits and infrastructure before committing to development, Agnico aims to produce more reliable cost estimates, reduce execution risks and strengthen investor confidence in its ability to deliver new mines. “Investors are okay to take risks if they feel they’ve been truthfully and objectively told what those risks are,” Al-Joundi said. “Investors, by definition, take risks. They won’t invest in someone they don’t trust.”
Staying inside budgets
Since grappling with cost overruns, Agnico has demonstrated its ability to deliver major projects within budget. Its Meliadine mine in Nunavut achieved commercial production in May 2019 ahead of schedule and about $70 million below its original $900-million construction budget. More recently, the company had completed 62% of detailed engineering when it approved construction of the Hope Bay gold project in Nunavut’s Kitikmeot region in May 2026, putting the project within the 60% to 70% range Al-Joundi described. By the end of September, engineering had advanced to approximately 76%, while construction was about 13% complete and slightly ahead of schedule. First gold production is targeted for 2030.
In-house talent
Agnico’s approach extends beyond engineering. Rather than relying entirely on outside contractors to build its mines, the company retains experienced construction teams that move between projects in the same mining regions. “In Nunavut, we are building our fourth mine. It’s the same team that built the previous three mines,” Al-Joundi said. “The people who build our shafts are our people.” He pointed to Canadian Malartic in Quebec, where the company plans to use personnel who worked on its first shaft to develop a second. Keeping experienced workers and construction expertise within the company reduces the need to assemble unfamiliar teams for each project. It also gives Agnico greater familiarity with local suppliers, infrastructure and construction costs, Al-Joundi said.
Not all roses
But he acknowledged Agnico’s approach isn’t perfect. It requires substantial upfront investment and can delay development announcements. “We have the cash flow to allow us to spend – making the numbers up – $100 million on engineering before we go ahead instead of $15 million,” he said. “We just have the luxury of being able to do that.” The benefits are particularly significant in Nunavut, where short shipping seasons and high transportation costs leave little room for construction mistakes, he said. At Hope Bay, Al-Joundi estimated that shipping materials by barge, such as structural steel, costs about 10¢ per kilogram, compared with roughly $10 per kilogram by air. The company has only about seven weeks to move supplies north by sea.

Jay Leno Sits in the Driver's Seat of the All-New Tesla Model Y L, Lets the Car Drive on Its Own
20 photos
Photo: Jay Leno's Garage | YouTube
Three rows, six seats, two motors, and six inches of extra legroom. This is the all-new Tesla Model Y L. The electric SUV went into production at Giga Texas back in September, and deliveries have just begun. That is the exact car that Jay Leno takes for a drive, but he doesn’t actually drive it.
The car that has just been parked in Jay Leno's Garage is a 2027 Tesla Model Y L with the Premium trim, finished in Cosmic Silver, a new exterior color, over a Zen Gray interior, which is a new interior color, and rides on 20-inch wheels.
It is one of the few hundred units that Tesla is "releasing into the wild" bearing the Launch Edition badge. Lars Moravy, Vice President of Vehicle Engineering, and Franz von Holzhausen, Head of Design, accompany the car on the show to dissect it on camera.
Tesla has offered a three-row version of the Model Y before as a $2,500 factory upgrade, but with no wheelbase extension, as the automaker squeezed two more seats into the existing trunk space, in which two adults could have only traveled in terribly contorted positions. As for the L version, it is not just a stretched version of the standard model.
Photo: Jay Leno's Garage | YouTube Now, the extended-wheelbase Tesla Model Y L is roughly 7 inches (179 millimeters) longer, which translates to 6 more inches of interior space. That makes enough space for two adults to travel comfortably in the third row.
That is also because the extended-wheelbase variant features a straightened rear quarter-panel roofline to maximize headroom in the back, a spoiler-integrated brake light, and a lower drag coefficient: 0.216 versus 0.220 for the standard model. This configuration is what Lars Moravy’s sister-in-law has been asking for long before it came out.
The Model Y L comes with a dual-motor powertrain pushing out 496 horsepower (503 metric horsepower) and 405 pound-feet (493 Newton meters) of torque. That is enough to make it flash from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in 4.4 seconds on its way to a top speed of 125 mph (201 kph). " Because you know we don't make slow cars, " Moravy brags.
An upgraded 83-kWh NMCA battery pack allows the vehicle to handle the extra 212 pounds of structural weight from the elongated wheelbase without sacrificing the brisk acceleration characteristic of the standard lineup.
Photo: Jay Leno's Garage | YouTube The battery stores enough energy for a drive of up to 332 miles (534 kilometers) before it needs to be plugged in again, when it rides on 19-inch wheels. When equipped with the 20-inch wheels, like this car is, it goes as far as 328 miles (528 kilometers) on a single charge .
Tesla has officially crossed the 10 million vehicle milestone at its Fremont, California factory. The milestone car was a black Model Y. Out of Tesla's 10.2 million vehicles delivered, the Tesla Model Y has surpassed 4.5 million lifetime sales globally.
With ten airbags and Full Self-Driving , the Model Y L, just like its siblings, stands as one of the safest cars out there. Once in the driver’s seat, Jay Leno doesn't need to touch anything. The car drives on its own, with no human interference whatsoever. But he does need to pay attention, because the system tracks the user’s eyesight through an integrated cabin-facing camera located directly above the rearview mirror.
The system continuously tracks your eyes to calculate where you are looking. If you glance away from the windshield to look at your phone, interact extensively with the center screen, or stare out the side windows, the system registers the divergence.
Photo: Jay Leno's Garage | YouTube In addition to eye gaze, the camera also evaluates the angle and tilt of your head to check for drowsiness or medical emergencies, monitoring if your head begins to droop. When FSD uses the vision system to gauge attention, a green indicator appears in the status bar on the main screen to show that camera monitoring is active.
For Tesla, putting the self-driving tech from the Cybercab in all of its vehicles is just a matter of time. " I have not touched the steering wheel since we left the garage," Leno admits. Lars Moravy says he traveled just like that for a record 80 miles (129 kilometers).
Now, with Leno in the driver's seat, the car pulls over to make room for an ambulance to pass, reacting far better than other drivers who don't move out of the way just as fast. However, a DUI is still a DUI in any Tesla, except for the Cybercab . The responsibility lies with the driver.
From the captain’s chair in the second row, the ride is more comfortable, with generous legroom and an integrated, fold-down padded armrest on the inside edge, mirroring the premium seating style found in the larger Model X.
Photo: Jay Leno's Garage | YouTube Both second-row seats feature multi-stage heating, integrated USB-C fast-charging ports built into the rear of the center console, and localized air vents connected to the vehicle's upgraded three-zone climate control system.
At some point, Leno asks about “a new S-Class,” actually referring to the Model S, but the final one rolled off the production line two months ago with no successor in sight. However, it is a never-say-never situation, Lars Moravy admits. But is there really a need or a demand for a sedan when you’ve got all you need in an SUV?
That one SUV that checks all the boxes starts at $61,990 in Launch Edition form. That is roughly $4,000 above the standard Model Y Performance ($57,990) and about $12,000 above a standard Model Y Long Range AWD.

source_document.body:
Agnico Eagle Mines chair Sean Boyd has been awarded The Northern Miner's earns the Lifetime Achievement Award.
By: Colin McClelland November 9, 2026
A takeover that brought Coeur Mining (TSX, NYSE: CDE) into Canada, a strategy connecting uranium production with reactor technology and four decades spent building a gold giant underpin The Northern Miner ’s latest leadership awards.
Coeur CEO Mitchell Krebs is Mining Person of the Year, Cameco (TSX: CCO; NYSE: CCJ) president and chief operating officer Grant Isaac receives Operator of the Year, and Agnico Eagle Mines (TSX, NYSE: AEM) chair Sean Boyd earns the Lifetime Achievement Award.
“It wasn’t really about, and hasn’t really been about, how big we are, how many mines we’ve built,” Boyd told The Northern Miner . “It’s more about how we did it, and just trying to do things the right way.”
The three honourees pursued different paths to growth. Each invested through industry cycles, strengthened existing operations and built teams that could sustain the business beyond any one transaction.
Krebs adds Canada
Boyd and Isaac are due to receive their awards on stage Nov. 29 at The Northern Miner ’s London Symposium . Krebs is set to receive his award at The Northern Miner ’s Rome Symposium , which runs May 26–27, 2027.
Coeur CEO Mitchell Krebs is The Northern Miner’s Mining Person of the Year.
For Krebs, the defining move was Coeur’s acquisition of New Gold, completed in March. The takeover added Rainy River in Ontario and New Afton in British Columbia, giving the Chicago-based producer its first operating Canadian mines and a substantial copper business.
The deal capped a rebuilding effort that began after Krebs became CEO in 2011. Moving the company out of Coeur d’Alene, Idaho, brought fresh ideas into a business with roots there dating back to the late 1920s, Krebs told The Northern Miner in an Oct. 16 interview. Coeur sold assets outside North America and reinvested in mines it decided to keep, including Rochester in Nevada.
The Rochester expansion strained Coeur’s finances, but as the enlarged silver-gold mine began to deliver, it gave the company the momentum to buy SilverCrest Metals, Krebs said. That acquisition, completed in February 2025, brought cash and the high-grade, lower-cost Las Chispas mine in Mexico. It helped Coeur repay debt and repair its balance sheet before buying New Gold.
Coeur recorded negative free cash flow of $297 million (C$416 million) in 2023. Krebs said in October he expected it to generate close to $1.5 billion in 2026, even with only nine months of contributions from the New Gold mines.
“Before we were consumers of capital, now we’re generators of a significant amount of cash flow, and our focus now is really turning to capital allocation with a much longer-term perspective,” Krebs said.
The immediate priority is integrating the acquisitions and finding more mineralization around existing mines. Coeur plans to spend about $158 million on exploration this year, almost 50% more than last year, Krebs said.
“I mean, it’s an extractive business, right?” he said. “So if you’re not finding more ounces, you need to be adding new ounces through external opportunities.”
Isaac builds demand
Cameco’s 49% interest in Westinghouse Electric connects its uranium operations with reactor technology, fuel fabrication and servicing. Helping utilities build reactors could create decades of demand for Cameco’s uranium and fuel services, Isaac told The Northern Miner in an October interview about the company’s growth strategy.
Cameco president and chief operating officer Grant Isaac receives The Northern Miner’s Operator of the Year award.
“Over the long run, the value of selling uranium for 80 to 100 years is way greater than the five to seven years of building a reactor,” Isaac said. “So think of it as our strategy is about not waiting for others to create new demand for us. We’re out there building our own demand.”
At its mines, Cameco bases production decisions on long-term contracts with utilities, Isaac said. At McArthur River in Saskatchewan, unexpected clay slowed the ground-freezing work needed to reach new mining areas. Management held off on spending heavily to recover lost time because customer commitments didn’t justify the cost, he said.
About 30% of Cameco’s licensed and built production capacity was either being held back or on care and maintenance, Isaac said. That gives the company room to increase output as utilities sign contracts.
Boyd’s lasting culture
Boyd’s recognition reflects Agnico’s transformation from a regional producer with one mine into Canada’s largest mining company. During his 24 years as CEO, its market value increased more than 100-fold.
His account begins with founder Paul Penna’s generosity and the relationships that persuaded a young auditor to join the company in 1985. As Boyd recalled in his Lifetime Achievement profile , that became Agnico’s “culture of the heart,” placing employees and communities alongside shareholder returns.
When safety concerns forced the closure of the Goldex mine in 2011, Agnico committed to paying employees for three months. During the 2013 gold price collapse, it took a measured approach to spending and jobs, preserving the strength to pursue subsequent opportunities.
Those included Canadian Malartic, while the 2022 Kirkland Lake Gold merger added Detour Lake, Macassa and Fosterville.
Asked what Penna would recognize today, Boyd returned to the company’s character.
“He’d recognize the feel,” Boyd said. “He’d be prouder of the fact that we did it in a way where it still feels the same.” Print

REGION: Canada
COMPANY: Agnico Eagle Mines Cameco Coeur Mining

2028 Ford Mustang Shelby GT350 Successor To Feature Dark Horse Branding
21 photos
Photo: Ford
Ford's next track-oriented Mustang is expected to get a manual tranny and naturally aspirated V8 goodness. According to documents that have presumably been sent by Ford to dealers nationwide, the long-awaited replacement of the Shelby GT350 is due to be revealed in late 2027.
That makes it a 2028 model by Ford Authority standards, and Ford Authority further understands that a relatively short production timeline is on the menu. Specifically, the yet-unnamed track pony should be gone after the 2029 model year, which doesn't make too much sense if you ask me.
S650 is what Ford calls the seventh-generation Mustang, which launched in 2023 for the 2024 model year. The previous generation was produced for model years 2015 through 2023, meaning that Ford's current Mustang still has plenty of years left. As for the Shelby GT350 per se, its last iteration was produced for model years 2015 through 2020. Fewer than 150 rolled off the line for 2015, though.
This, in turn, makes 2016 the first retail model year. All told, five retail model years for the Shelby GT350 versus two for its replacement seems a bit kooky. In any case, Ford Authority further learned that Dark Horse SC-like widebody goodies are on the menu for the newcomer.
To be offered in fastback-only flavor, the mysterious new track weapon is apparently getting a large V8. The cited publication is pointing toward either 5.2 or 5.4 liters, which raises more questions than it answers. Although the 5.2 has the most obvious connection to the GT350, the 5.4 would make a connection to the GT3 racing program and the WEC hypercar.
Photo: Ford Referred to as Voodoo, the 5.2 flat-plane V8 of the GT350 made 526 horsepower and 429 pound-feet (582 Newton-meters) at full chatter. It was only available with a Tremec-sourced manual transmission capable of handling the naturally aspirated engine's redline. Another Ford engine with this displacement is the cross-plane Aluminator, a crate engine with forged internals.
Further gifted with a Cobra Jet intake manifold and GT350 heads, the Aluminator 5.2 XS develops 580 horsepower and 445 pound-feet (603 Newton-meters) on premium-grade dinosaur juice. Being a crate engine, the Aluminator has very slim chances of powering the GT350's replacement.
As for the GT3 and WEC racing engines, both of them share the Coyote architecture. The Mustang GT3 lump was developed in collaboration with M-Sport with no hybrid assistance whatsoever. It uses dry-sump lubrication, a Bosch Motorsport control unit, and its transmission is an Xtrac-supplied racing unit.
As for the hypercar's engine, that one was developed specifically for the ORECA-based prototype and its LMDh-spec hybrid system. Whatever V8 it may get, its free-breathing nature and manual tranny will do the talking.
Ford Authority expects the Dark Horse branding to remain somewhere in the model's identity. The Dearborn-based automaker has already secured the rights to use Dark Horse Boss in 2025, and that's our best guess yet.

Server
Accelerators
google tpu 8tx board illustration
Google is expanding its eighth-generation TPU portfolio with two new offerings, the TPU 8tx and the TPU 8i Max. This marks the first time Google has introduced four distinct system configurations in a single year, though it is not four new chip designs. The 8tx builds on existing silicon for confidential computing, marking a notable win for AMD, while the 8i Max combines two 8i chips into one package to tackle massive context windows.
Google TPU 8x
When we covered the TPU v8s at Hot Chips 2026 , we highlighted how Google specialized networking for different workloads. The inference-focused TPU 8i uses a Boardfly topology with a maximum network-hop diameter of seven, compared to sixteen hops in the training-oriented torus design. This structural difference reduces latency for real-time reasoning, helping explain why Google continues to tailor interconnects rather than rely on a single fabric.
Google TPUv8 Hot Chips 2026 TPU8i Boardfly Network
The TPU 8tx is the third system in the generation and targets regulated enterprises and governments running frontier or proprietary models alongside sensitive data. It uses the same silicon as the training-focused TPU 8t, but Google has paired it with custom 5th Gen AMD EPYC “Turin” hosts to build security directly into the hardware layer. Normally, data is encrypted at rest and in transit but must be unlocked in memory while a computer processes it. The 8tx keeps that active data protected through confidential computing , which encrypts data in use inside an isolated trusted execution environment.
Here is Google’s rendering of the TPU 8tx board. The illustration shows four accelerator chips with heat sinks and connector ports along one edge, giving a sense of the tray layout that pairs these accelerators with their Turin host CPUs.
google tpu 8tx board illustration
For the 8tx host CPU, Google selected 5th Gen AMD EPYC Turin to match the TPU 8t’s PCIe Gen5 x16 interface. A dual-socket Turin configuration provides 128 Gen5 lanes, ensuring zero I/O oversubscription across four TPUs and high-speed NICs. Google noted that a Gen6 host like AMD EPYC Venice (stay tuned for more on that) would step down to Gen5 speeds without adding accelerator bandwidth, aligning with their 2027 hardware qualification schedule.
The 8tx also adopts the Boardfly network from the inference-oriented TPU 8i rather than the training-optimized torus. That topology reduces the maximum hops between chips, which matters for multi-step agents that make many sequential inference calls. Google claims up to 2x lower latency than TPU 8t with a near-zero performance penalty.
Google TPU 8i Max Packs Two Chips and More Memory
The fourth system, TPU 8i Max, attacks the memory wall from a different angle. When many agents work across an entire codebase or hours of video simultaneously, memory bandwidth becomes the bottleneck before compute does. Google combined two low-latency TPU 8i chips into a single multi-chip package.
That gives the 8i Max double the compute, double the SRAM, and double the HBM bandwidth of a single TPU 8i. Specifically, it offers 384 GB of high-bandwidth memory, about a third more than the TPU 8i, while HBM bandwidth doubles to 17.2TB/s and on-chip SRAM doubles to 768 MB. The TPU 8i Max doubles HBM bandwidth to 17.2 TB/s and on-chip SRAM to 768 MB, directly addressing the memory wall that bottlenecks large-context agentic workloads.
Google TPU 8 hardware spec comparison chart
We asked and Google told us that if data must remain within the confidential computing domain, users should stick with TPU 8tx for inference and serving. This system retains the same low-latency Boardfly topology optimized for real-time tasks.
Final Words
Probably the key message here is that Google is tailoring its TPU offerings for different parts of the AI stack, and really even different customers. The TPU 8tx seems to be more of a customized product for confidential computing, while the TPU 8i Max is designed for inference. For AMD, this is probably not going to drive a 10% server CPU market share gain overnight. Instead, it is a big win because AMD is notching both a win for EPYC in a non-AMD accelerator system, and it is showing its confidential computing chops by winning a socket at a major hyperscaler.

EICMA 2026 • Yamaha Births New Adventure Scooter Family, Three RW Models That Look More Like Motorcycles
There Is One Chinese Automaker That Is Inching Closer to the U.S. Market
11 photos
Photo: Jaecoo
Chinese automakers are knocking at the doors of the American car market one way or another, and Canada seems to be the password to entry. Chery Automobile Co. is exploring local manufacturing options in Canada as it prepares to launch vehicle sales there. Direct access to the U.S. market remains uncertain due to strict tariffs and software restrictions.
Chery is inching closer to its debut on the Canadian market, scheduled to take place in early 2027. In the meantime, it is struggling to find a shortcut into the United States. Executive Vice President Guibing Zhang explained that Chery is even considering setting up a local plant or taking over idle plant capacity and working with partners to achieve this target.
While a presence in Canada raises massive concerns about the already existing tensions with Washington, which imposes a prohibitive 100% tariff on Chinese EVs, Zhang noted that Canada is valuable enough for the automaker to justify local manufacturing, even if access to the U.S. market is never possible.
However, Canadian manufacturing would require meeting local labor standards, building domestic supply chains and offering secure software systems. Meanwhile, Canada shifted its trade policy by canceling its 100% tax on Chinese vehicles, which opens the door for high-tech cars at affordable prices.
Under a trade agreement brokered by Prime Minister Mark Carney, Canada replaced the tariff with a targeted quota system, which allows up to 49,000 EVs or hybrids built in China into Canada annually.
Photo: Jaecoo For these vehicles, Chinese automakers would pay the baseline tariff rate of only 6.1% instead of the huge 100% or over. The number limits of vehicles will step up progressively to roughly 63,000 units per year by 2030.
This move marks a strict policy departure from the United States. In the meantime, American-built vehicles entering the Canadian market will continue to face a 25% tariff, prompting automakers like Tesla to supply Canada from Shanghai and Germany instead of its U.S. plants.
This is the context in which Chery is launching its export-focused sub-brands, Omoda and Jaecoo, in Canada through its newly registered entity, Omoda & Jaecoo Canada Inc. The launch was originally scheduled for late 2026. Now, Chery Vice President Charlie Zhang has just confirmed that the brand launch is scheduled for early 2027, as reported by Bloomberg.
In the meantime, the company is planning to open roughly a dozen dealerships across Quebec, Ontario, and British Columbia, aiming for 6,000 unit sales in its first full year on the Canadian market.
Photo: Omoda Test vehicles operating with Ontario manufacturer plates have already been spotted around the Greater Toronto Area. The Omoda 9 , which is a plug-in hybrid with 450 horsepower, and the Jaecoo J5 electric SUV will be two key players on the Canadian market.
Pricing has yet to be disclosed. However, the Jaecoo J5 is expected to start at around 36,000 Canadian dollars, which translates to roughly US$25,500. In the meantime, the Omoda 9 should kick off at approximately 48,000 Canadian dollars ($34,000). The two models are already on the market in Europe and Australia .
Chinese-manufactured vehicles do not qualify for Canada’s federal Electric Vehicle Affordability Program (EVAP), which brings incentives of up to 5,000 Canadian dollars to electric vehicles.
